name: ACF Framework Charts — handoff inventory
note: Representative/illustrative exhibits. visualDataMode + disclosure define how each chart is presented. See README-agency-chart-handoff.md.

charts.title: Shape the Payoff
charts.frameworkClaim: ACF shapes exposure: the left side is capped, the right side is left free to run.
charts.readerTakeaway: Survive the left tail; stay convex on the right tail.
charts.chartType: Conceptual payoff curve vs a symmetric reference line.
charts.setupLine: The payoff shape the whole framework is built to produce
charts.explainerHeadline: The framework is a payoff shape, not a prediction.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Bend the Tail
charts.frameworkClaim: ACF truncates the left tail and extends the right tail of the outcome distribution.
charts.readerTakeaway: Same center of gravity, deliberately reshaped tails.
charts.chartType: Conceptual outcome-distribution reshape vs a symmetric reference.
charts.setupLine: ACF reshapes the distribution of outcomes, it does not just chase higher returns
charts.explainerHeadline: We reshape the outcomes, not the average.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: The Window Opens
charts.frameworkClaim: ACF waits for setups where downside is defined and upside can accelerate.
charts.readerTakeaway: Patience through compression; size into confirmation; let the release run.
charts.chartType: Representative regime/path chart with a compression field and release marker.
charts.setupLine: Compression, then confirmation, then asymmetric release
charts.explainerHeadline: Convexity is a window, not a constant.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

charts.title: Capital Has Weather
charts.frameworkClaim: Portfolio construction changes with the macro regime.
charts.readerTakeaway: You are not allocating in a vacuum; you are allocating into weather.
charts.chartType: Growth × inflation quadrant with a representative regime path.
charts.setupLine: Same assets, different regime, different behaviour
charts.explainerHeadline: The same portfolio behaves differently in different weather.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Regime-agnostic allocation as a failure mode

charts.title: Govern the Thesis
charts.frameworkClaim: ACF is a closed-loop operating system, not a fixed set of weights.
charts.readerTakeaway: Every position is traceable to a thesis and governed by a tripwire.
charts.chartType: Minimal flow/loop diagram of the framework control system.
charts.setupLine: Thesis creates exposure · exposure creates risk · tripwires govern behaviour
charts.explainerHeadline: Structure flows from a thesis and is governed by tripwires.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

sources.label: Order of operations · the closed loop

charts.title: The Hedge Broke
charts.frameworkClaim: Stocks and bonds are not always true diversifiers.
charts.readerTakeaway: When inflation drives the regime, the hedge can fall with the risk.
charts.chartType: Indexed-return stress chart, 3 series (stocks, bonds, 60/40).
charts.setupLine: Indexed total return through an inflation shock: stocks, bonds, and the 60/40 blend
charts.explainerHeadline: The hedge can fail with the risk.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Bloomberg US Aggregate total return (ICE proxy)

charts.title: Correlation Turns
charts.frameworkClaim: Stock–bond correlation changes when inflation becomes the dominant stress.
charts.readerTakeaway: The diversifier did not disappear. The regime that produced it did.
charts.chartType: Rolling 24-month stock–bond correlation with a non-rectangular inflation-shock background.
charts.setupLine: Rolling 24-month stock–bond correlation across an inflation-shock window
charts.explainerHeadline: When inflation runs the regime, correlations flip.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Bloomberg US Aggregate total return (ICE proxy)

charts.title: Inflation Was Bigger
charts.frameworkClaim: CPI alone does not capture the full inflation story.
charts.readerTakeaway: Consumer prices roughly doubled. The assets that store capital did far more.
charts.chartType: Three normalized index lines with a gap area between assets and CPI.
charts.setupLine: CPI, housing, and a broad-asset proxy, each indexed to 100
charts.explainerHeadline: The CPI tells one story; capital saw another.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: S&P/Case-Shiller US National Home Price Index

charts.title: The Bill Came Due
charts.frameworkClaim: Debt and interest burden reduce policy freedom.
charts.readerTakeaway: For decades, debt rose while falling rates hid the cost. The cost is no longer hidden.
charts.chartType: Stacked dual-panel chart, shared timeline. Top: debt/GDP. Bottom: net interest/GDP.
charts.setupLine: Federal debt and net interest, both as a share of GDP, on a shared timeline
charts.explainerHeadline: The cost of debt stopped being free.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Federal debt held by the public / GDP

charts.title: Path Changes Everything
charts.frameworkClaim: Same average return, opposite sequence, opposite survival outcome.
charts.readerTakeaway: Withdrawal-phase capital does not care about the average. It cares about the order.
charts.chartType: Two-path sequence-of-returns simulation.
charts.setupLine: Identical return set, opposite order, $1.0M start, $40k annual withdrawals
charts.explainerHeadline: Same returns. Opposite outcomes.
charts.disclosure: Representative simulation · Built to show path dependency, not a historical backtest

sources.label: Identical annual return set, opposite order

charts.title: Survive the Path
charts.frameworkClaim: Upside only matters if sizing lets you survive the path.
charts.readerTakeaway: Volatile assets can still compound — through, not around, the drawdown.
charts.chartType: Invested-vs-value representative path with drawdown shading.
charts.setupLine: Cumulative invested versus portfolio value, with drawdown-from-peak shaded
charts.explainerHeadline: Compounding happens through the drawdown.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Constant DCA, no rebalancing, no leverage

charts.title: Method Before Macro
charts.frameworkClaim: The framework’s method persists across regimes; the macro thesis changes with the environment.
charts.readerTakeaway: Keep the method fixed; let the thesis move.
charts.chartType: Two stacked panels: a rotating macro-thesis line over a stable method baseline.
charts.setupLine: The lineage holds steady while the macro thesis rotates with the regime
charts.explainerHeadline: The method is constant; the thesis rotates.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Ruin Comes First
charts.frameworkClaim: Fragility is nonlinear and ruin is irreversible; survival must precede optimization.
charts.readerTakeaway: You cannot compound from zero.
charts.chartType: Two outcome paths with similar volatility but different left-tail ruin.
charts.setupLine: Two portfolios, similar volatility, very different left tails
charts.explainerHeadline: Survival is not one goal among many.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Conviction Needs an Exit
charts.frameworkClaim: Concentration only works when paired with monitoring and disciplined exits.
charts.readerTakeaway: Size up on conviction, but keep the exit.
charts.chartType: Position size versus conviction, with and without an enforced exit cap.
charts.setupLine: Position size can scale with conviction only because an exit caps the downside
charts.explainerHeadline: Concentration is earned by the exit.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Markets Feed Back
charts.frameworkClaim: Prices do not only reflect fundamentals; they can change fundamentals.
charts.readerTakeaway: Price is an input, not just an output.
charts.chartType: Reflexive loop of price, capital, fundamentals, and validation.
charts.setupLine: Price → capital → fundamentals → validation, and back to price
charts.explainerHeadline: Price can write the fundamentals it claims to read.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Time Changes Prudence
charts.frameworkClaim: Longer horizons change what counts as prudent; tax-free compounding and convex exposure become more important.
charts.readerTakeaway: A long horizon rewrites the prudent choice.
charts.chartType: Two compounding paths diverging at long horizon (simulation).
charts.setupLine: Conventional versus convex, tax-free compounding over a 70-year horizon
charts.explainerHeadline: Prudence is a function of horizon.
charts.disclosure: Representative simulation · Built to show path dependency, not a historical backtest

charts.title: Capital Finds the Bottleneck
charts.frameworkClaim: A valid thesis must map structural force into capital-flow pathways.
charts.readerTakeaway: Trace the force to its bottleneck to its instruments.
charts.chartType: Flow map: structural force → bottlenecks → where capital lands.
charts.setupLine: A structural force only matters where it is constrained — that is where capital lands
charts.explainerHeadline: Force is not a trade; the bottleneck is.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Narrative Is Not Thesis
charts.frameworkClaim: A valid macro thesis needs persistence, capital-flow implications, falsifiability, and multi-year runway.
charts.readerTakeaway: Most narratives never make it through the gates.
charts.chartType: Validation gauntlet: narrative through four gates to a thesis.
charts.setupLine: A story becomes a thesis only after it survives four gates
charts.explainerHeadline: A narrative is a candidate, not a conclusion.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Phase Changes Sizing
charts.frameworkClaim: A thesis can remain structurally valid while its deployment phase changes sizing and risk posture.
charts.readerTakeaway: Right thesis, wrong size, still a loss.
charts.chartType: Thesis validity held constant while sizing rises then trims across phases.
charts.setupLine: The same valid thesis carries different sizing early, mid, and late
charts.explainerHeadline: Validity is not a sizing instruction.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Liquidity Sets the Tide
charts.frameworkClaim: In the current thesis, liquidity cycles shape Bitcoin and long-duration asset sensitivity.
charts.readerTakeaway: Convex assets ride the liquidity tide, magnified.
charts.chartType: Representative liquidity impulse versus convex-asset sensitivity.
charts.setupLine: A representative liquidity impulse and the convex asset that amplifies it
charts.explainerHeadline: Convex assets trade the tide, not the weather.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Representative liquidity impulse vs convex sensitivity

charts.title: Power Law Holds
charts.frameworkClaim: Bitcoin’s long-term path can be contextualized by power-law behavior — a regime heuristic, not a prediction.
charts.readerTakeaway: A map of where Bitcoin sits on its adoption curve, not a forecast.
charts.chartType: Log power-law corridor with price oscillating between euphoria and capitulation bands.
charts.setupLine: Price against a log power-law corridor — central tendency, with euphoria and capitulation bands
charts.explainerHeadline: Power-law bands map the regime; they do not predict it.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Power-law bands as a regime heuristic

charts.title: One Asset, Ten Tests
charts.frameworkClaim: Bitcoin uniquely satisfies the framework’s requirements for a convexity backbone asset.
charts.readerTakeaway: No alternative clears all ten at once.
charts.chartType: Requirement × asset scorecard (meets / partial / fails).
charts.setupLine: The ten backbone requirements, scored across candidate reserve assets
charts.explainerHeadline: Ten requirements, derived from the objective — not reverse-engineered.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Volatility Is the Toll
charts.frameworkClaim: Bitcoin volatility is the cost of convexity; sizing decides whether it is survivable.
charts.readerTakeaway: The drawdown is the price of admission, not a reason to avoid it.
charts.chartType: Representative Bitcoin path with deep drawdowns vs the calmer total-portfolio line at managed size.
charts.setupLine: Large Bitcoin drawdowns, small total-portfolio impact at a managed allocation
charts.explainerHeadline: The volatility is the toll, not the risk.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Volatility as the cost of convexity; sizing for survivability

charts.title: Exposure Is Not Control
charts.frameworkClaim: 100% Bitcoin can win one favorable cycle; the framework optimizes for control across many.
charts.readerTakeaway: Max exposure wins the clean bull case; control wins the messy path.
charts.chartType: Interactive path-aware comparison: all three strategies through a drawdown, with an optional shock.
charts.setupLine: Choose the path. Then change the shock.
charts.explainerHeadline: Winning a cycle is not the same as staying in control.
charts.disclosure: Representative simulation · Built to show path dependency, not a historical backtest

sources.label: Max-exposure vs architected reserve across a cycle
Operational control across cycles and life events

charts.title: Models Must Converge
charts.frameworkClaim: Power-law, realized price, production cost, and liquidity models are most useful when they converge.
charts.readerTakeaway: Agreement strengthens conviction; disagreement is the signal.
charts.chartType: Valuation envelope — the spread between models narrows on convergence, widens on divergence.
charts.setupLine: The valuation models are most useful where they agree; divergence signals caution
charts.explainerHeadline: Conviction lives where the models agree.
charts.disclosure: Representative framework exhibit · Sources support the underlying concept

sources.label: Multi-model valuation: power-law, realized price, production cost, liquidity

charts.title: Accumulate, Don’t Trade
charts.frameworkClaim: Valuation models guide accumulation pacing and conviction, not selling the reserve.
charts.readerTakeaway: For an accumulator, a drawdown is a unit-accumulation window.
charts.chartType: Representative valuation heartbeat with DCA unit pulses: more units when cheap, framework leans in, never sells.
charts.setupLine: Bitcoin’s volatility is a heartbeat — the same dollars buy more units when it dips
charts.explainerHeadline: Volatility is not only pain — it buys units.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

sources.label: Accumulation pacing and the never-sell reserve

charts.title: Cold Storage to Borrow
charts.frameworkClaim: The Bitcoin reserve moves from accumulation to collateralized borrowing without forced sale.
charts.readerTakeaway: Liquidity comes from borrowing against the reserve, not selling it.
charts.chartType: Reserve lifecycle flow: accumulate → self-custody → mature → collateralized loan → liquidity.
charts.setupLine: The reserve lifecycle: accumulate, self-custody, mature, borrow — without a forced sale
charts.explainerHeadline: Liquidity without selling the reserve.
charts.disclosure: Conceptual diagram · Illustrative framework exhibit, not historical data

charts.title: Reserve Share Evolves
charts.frameworkClaim: A 10–15% reserve can evolve into a 30–50% mature share, at which point borrow-phase governance matters.
charts.readerTakeaway: Success changes the job: from accumulating to governing the reserve.
charts.chartType: Reserve share as a percent of net worth, rising through target, elevated, and mature phases.
charts.setupLine: A 10–15% reserve can mature into a 30–50% share, where borrow-phase governance begins
charts.explainerHeadline: The reserve outgrows its target — on purpose.
charts.disclosure: Representative simulation · Built to show path dependency, not a historical backtest

sources.label: Reserve share evolving via accumulation + appreciation
